body.p: Applicant submits this Reply in response to the Final Office Action mailed October 18, 2023.
I. Status of the Claims
By this Reply, Applicant amends claims 1, 9, and 17. The originally filed
specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended and new claims. Claims 1-20 are pending in this application. Claims 1, 9, and 17 are the sole independent claims.
II. Interview
Applicant thanks Examiner Alter for the courtesies extended during the

telephonic interview of December 5, 2023. The remarks provided below are consistent with the issues discussed and agreements reached during the interview. During the interview, the parties discussed the pending rejections in detail. III. Section 112(a) Rejections

In the Office Action, claims 1-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) for allegedly failing to comply with the written description requirement. (Office Action at pages 2-4.) Applicant does not necessarily agree with this rejection. However, in order to further the prosecution of this application, Applicant has amended claims 1, 9, and 17 to address the concern raised in the Office Action. In particular, the claims are amended to remove the phrase "receiving a threshold blood flow characteristic associated with the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel." The amended claims further recite "generating and displaying (i) an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to a tissue region of the patient's

bowel, or (ii) a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's bowel based on a comparison of the calculated blood flow characteristic to a predetermined threshold blood flow characteristic." (Emphasis added.) These features find support in at least paragraphs [0046]-[0048] of the present specification as published. In view of this, Applicant requests that this § 112 rejection be withdrawn. IV. Section 112(b) Rejections

In the Office Action, claims 1-20 were rejected as indefinite under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b} based on the use of the phrase "associated with" in claims 1, 9, and 17. (Office Action at pages 3-4.) While Applicant does not agree that the phrase "associated with" renders the claims unclear, to further prosecution, claims 1, 9, and 17 are amended herein to remove this phrase. The amended claims are, therefore, clear and definite. Reconsideration of this rejection is requested. V. Section 103 Rejections

In the Office Action, claims 1-7, 9-15, and 17-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as being allegedly unpatentable over Taylor (US 2012/0041318) in view of non- patent literature entitled "Mesenteric vasculature and collateral pathways" by Walker (Seminars in interventional radiology vol. 26, 3 (2009): 167-74) and John et al. (US 2007/0208263). (Office Action at pages 4-16.) Claims 8, and 16 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as being allegedly unpatentable over Taylor in view of Walker and John, in view of non-patent literature entitled "Intestinal Ischemic Syndrome" by Cleveland Clinic (https://my.clevelandclinic.org/services/heart/disorders/arterial- disease/intestinal-ischemic-syndrome). (Office Action at pages 4-18.) The rejections are respectfully traversed.
Claim 1 recites:
determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the
patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific
anatomical model, based on a determined mass of the
portion of the patient's bowel, amount of visceral vasculature
and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood to the portion of
patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model, and the received physiological state of the
patient
That is, "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific anatomical model" is based on all of:
" a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel,
" amount of visceral vasculature and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood
to the portion of patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient- specific anatomic model, and
" the received physiological state of the patient.

In rejecting claim 1, the Office Action asserts that paragraphs [0224], [0227], and [0232] of Taylor disclose "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific anatomical model, based on a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel." (Office Action at page 6.) The Office Action points to other portions of Taylor as disclosing "amount of visceral vasculature and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood to the portion of patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model." (Office Action at pages 6-7.) These portions of Taylor do not disclose these elements in combination.
For example, paragraph [0224] of states:
The method 600 may include determining a condition by
calculating, using the ventricular or myocardial mass
calculated in step 631, a resting coronary flow based on the
relationship Q=QoMa, where a is a preset scaling exponent, M is the ventricular or myocardial mass, and Qo is a preset
constant (e.g., as described above in connection with
determining the lumped parameter model in step 310 of FIG.
3) (step 632). Alternatively, the relationship may have the
form QocQoMa, as described above in connection with
determining the lumped parameter model in step 310 of FIG.

However, this portion of Taylor does not disclose that the determination includes "amount of visceral vasculature and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood to the portion of patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model" or "the received physiological state of the patient." Paragraph [0227] of Taylor relates to physical conditions of the patient. Paragraph [0232] of Taylor relates to a physician prescribing treatments to the patient based on a cFFR model. Other portions of Taylor disclose similar calculations for brain mass (paragraphs 0335] et seq.).
With respect to collateral pathway(s), the Office Action points to portions of

Taylor relating to "the potential for collateral pathways for supplying adequate blood flow for the patient" in paragraphs [0244], [0340], and [0348]. (Office Action at page 7.) However, each of these portions state: "The model may also be modified to simulate the effect of preventing blood flow through certain arteries in order to predict the potential for collateral pathways for supplying adequate blood flow for the patient." (Emphasis added.) That is, these portions relate to a prediction of future collateral pathways and not a determination of a blood flow demand based on existing collateral pathways, as in claim 1.

Therefore, Taylor at most discloses "determining a blood flow demand ... based on ...a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel," but does not disclose "determining a blood flow demand ... based on ... amount of visceral vasculature and

collateral pathway(s)" or "determining a blood flow demand ... based on ... the received physiological state of the patient." These features of claim 1 recites all three elements in combination, and accordingly, Taylor does not disclose the features of claim 1. The remaining cited references fail to compensate for the noted deficiencies of Taylor and therefore, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over the cited references for at least these reasons.

In the Response to Arguments at page 19, the Office Action states: "In regards to the rejection under 35 USC 103 and in response to applicant's arguments against only the Taylor reference, one cannot show nonobviousness by attacking an individual reference where the rejections are based on combinations of references." Applicant disagrees with this characterization for at least two reasons. First, only a single reference, Taylor is cited with respect to these features of claim 1. Neither Walker nor John is cited with respect to these features. Thus, this portion of the rejection is not "based on combinations of references." Second, as discussed above, these features of claim 1 include a combination of elements in conjunction, not in the alternative. The cited portions of the sole cited reference, Taylor, at most disclose these elements separately. Accordingly, these disclosures can, at most, be interpreted to disclose these elements in the alternative.

The above comments are specifically directed to independent claim 1. However, it is respectfully submitted that the comments would be helpful in understanding various differences of the other independent claims over the cited references. Therefore, it is
respectfully submitted that all the independent claims are patentable over the cited references. Moreover, it is respectfully submitted that the various dependent claims are
patentable over the cited references for at least the reason that they depend from an independent claim that is patentable over the cited references.
In view of the above, it is respectfully submitted that the rejection is overcome. VI. Conclusion

The Office Action contains characterizations of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be

understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.
Applicant respectfully requests that this Reply under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116 be

entered by the Examiner, placing the claims in condition for allowance. The proposed claim amendments do not raise new issues or necessitate the undertaking of any additional search of the art by the Examiner. Therefore, this Reply should allow for immediate action by the Examiner.
Furthermore, Applicant respectfully points out that the final Office Action

presented new arguments as to the application of the art against the pending claims. It is respectfully submitted that the entering of this Reply would allow Applicant to respond to the final rejection and place the application in condition for allowance.
Finally, Applicant submits that the entry of this Reply would place the application in better form for appeal, should the Examiner dispute the patentability of the pending claims.

In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
If the examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution,
the examiner is invited to call applicant's undersigned representative at (202) 808-3563.

Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5906. In addition, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees due and any other fees due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 during the pendency of this application to Deposit Account No. 50-5906.
Respectfully submitted,
